master:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create ONE high-quality standalone anatomical exercise image: frame 1, SET UP, of a bilateral bodyweight FLOOR GLUTE BRIDGE, intended for a six-frame app sequence. Input image 1 is the CANONICAL ATHLETE AND LINEWORK reference; input image 2 is an additional reference for the same athlete in a reclining landscape composition. Preserve this exact bald, faceless, muscular white/light-grey male identity, white shoes, fine charcoal contours, crisp polished 2D anatomical shading and body proportions. Do not copy either reference's exercise or equipment.
Canvas: landscape 1536x1024, pure black background. Slightly elevated side three-quarter view, head at LEFT and feet at RIGHT, full body and both shoes clearly visible with comfortable margins. ONE person lying SUPINE ON THE FLOOR in the bridge STARTING position: head and shoulder blades resting naturally on the floor, pelvis resting on floor, knees bent approximately 90 degrees, feet hip-width apart and BOTH complete soles firmly planted on the same floor plane. Arms comfortably straight beside trunk with BOTH palms down on floor. Neutral relaxed neck, face directed up; no neck flexion. Show the near lateral buttock and back of thigh clearly enough for the muscle key. Anatomically plausible joint connections, exactly two arms and two legs, no displaced or duplicate knees.
Muscle map: visible gluteus maximus regions deepest saturated purple, visible hamstrings lighter lilac, a very subtle pale abdominal stabilizer tint. Preserve muscle sizes; clean white-grey body elsewhere. Do NOT shade the chest, biceps, quadriceps or shoulders bright purple. No see-through skin, no organs, no genitals.
This master establishes fixed head, shoulder contact, palms, both sole positions, camera and scale for all later bridge frames. Keep an uncluttered framing with adequate room above hips for their later elevation. No bench, dumbbells, barbell, band, mat edges, props, text, captions, arrows, labels, logos, border, panels or contact sheet. Return exactly ONE full-resolution image.
early:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific-educational. Edit this exact anatomical GLUTE BRIDGE master into frame 2, BEGIN LIFT. Same 1536x1024 canvas, black background, side three-quarter camera, same one athlete and all original linework and purple hierarchy. Lift ONLY the pelvis a small early amount, about one quarter of the way toward a full bridge (roughly 50-60 image pixels upward). Hips just clear the floor. Raise hips through hip extension; naturally rotate thighs and knees while preserving femur and tibia lengths and the original ankle/foot contacts. Keep ribs down; do not arch lumbar spine. This is an early lift, not the top bridge.
PIXEL-LOCK the head and ear, neck resting orientation, shoulder contact patches, the entire visible arms and palms on the floor, BOTH shoes and their floor contact positions, and all background pixels outside the moving torso/pelvis/thigh/knee region. Do not move, rescale, redraw or relight these fixed areas. Maintain near and far leg identity, stance width, two arms/two legs, shoe dimensions and identical body proportions. Chest/shoulders/arms remain white-grey, glutes saturated purple, hamstrings lilac, subtle pale abdomen. No added muscle bulk, no outlines getting softer, no extra equipment, no text or arrows. Return ONE full-resolution frame with the exact original crop.
